units.translation: The name Ἀραβίας [Arabia] has been left untouched in the copies, except that in some it is written, as often in manuscripts, 'Αρραβίας [Arrabia]. Yet it is foreign to this passage, not only for geographical reasons, which the older scholiast in the Medicean codex already touched upon, but also for metrical reasons. For since in the strophic verse a cretic Κολχίδος [of Colchis] is read, it is not likely that in the antistrophe a resolved form was used by Aeschylus. Schuetz seemed to himself to remedy the earlier fault by restoring Χαλυβίας [Chalybia], which he thought was the name of a Scythian city, deceived by the corrupt reading Χαλυβία [Chalybia] in the scholium on Apollonius Rhodius 2, 373, to which Holstenius had already restored the correct Χαδησία [Chadesia] in Stephanus of Byzantium p. 351: but both faults are removed by Heimsoeth's conjecture Χαλκίδος [of Chalcis], which was a city of Scythia, whose name not only Stephanus noted p. 684, 18 ed. Mein. (ἔστι καὶ πόλις Χαλκὶς ἐν Σκυθίᾳ, ἧς οἱ πολῖται Χαλκῖται καὶ ἡ χώρα Χαλκῖτις, ὡς Ερμείας ἐν περιηγήσει [there is also a city Chalcis in Scythia, whose citizens are Chalcitae and the region Chalcitia, as Hermeias in the Periegesis]), but also Hesychius indicated, Χαλκιδική: τα μέταλλα τοῦ σιδήρου ἐκεῖ πρῶτον εὑρεθέντα [Chalcidice: the mines of iron first discovered there], where Schrevelius compared Χαλκιδικὰς σπάθας [Chalcidian swords] of Alcman in Athenaeus 14 p. 627 B. To this city, therefore, the Aeschylean description fits best: ὑψίκρημνον οἳ πόλισμα Καυκάσου πέλας νέμονται, δάϊος στρατὸς ὀξυπρώροισι βρέμων ἐν αἰχμαῖς [who inhabit a high-cliffed city near the Caucasus, a hostile army roaring with sharp-prowed spears]. Since partly similar are the things which Strabo 16 p. 753 reports about Chalcis in Arabia (μετὰ δὲ τὸν Μάκραν ἐστὶν ὁ Μασσύας, ἔχων τινὰ καὶ ὀρεινά, ἐν οἷς ἡ Χαλκίς, ὥσπερ ἀκρόπολις τοῦ Μασσύου [after the Macra is the Massyas, having some mountainous parts, in which is Chalcis, as it were the acropolis of the Massyas]), some old glossator could have mistakenly written Αραβίας [Arabia] for Aeschylus's Χαλκίδος [of Chalcis], and later it was introduced into the text by others. Much more frequently the Χάλυβες [Chalybes], Scythians, and the iron Χαλυβδικόν [Chalybdic] (as in this very play 134 715. Sept. 728) are mentioned, about which I have spoken in the Thesaurus vol. 8 p. 1284.
